# The website

This folder is served as [eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/START.html). Everything in it runs in the browser. A recording you open is read on your own computer and goes nowhere.

| Page | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| [`START.html`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/START.html) | The start page. The finding so far, invented examples to try, and a list that matches each open dataset to the page that reads it. |
| [`index.html`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/index.html) | NeuroTranslator, the app. It shows a recording on its own clock, lines several recordings up on a shared clock, and replays a palm trial against the fitted palm models. |
| Fourteen folders, from `cemhsey-arrays/` to `wrist-replay/` (excluding the other readers listed below) | The study readers of the numbered table, one per folder. Each reads a recording of the kind one study used and runs that study's forecasts on it, or shows the study's results. |
| [`hand-search/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/hand-search/) | Type a sentence and find the moment of a recorded hand movement it describes, with the fitted models of [a newer study](../benchmarks/hand-language-retrieval/). Its [`forecast.html`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/hand-search/forecast.html) forecasts how far a wrist moves in the second after an instructor stops speaking ([its study](../benchmarks/preceding-instructions/)). |
| [`shared-motion/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/shared-motion/) | The general model's shared fit, which forecasts how far a tracked wrist or rat moves in about a quarter of a second, and the two angles of a wrist from its movement, with forearm and scalp signals if they are given, with or without a correction from four forearm signals, both knee angles of a walker from four seconds of earlier angles, the turning moment at each knee from four seconds of leg angles, the force under a walker's right foot, where one marker on the skin will be 200 milliseconds later, and how three sensors on an arm change after an instruction such as "bend my right elbow", fitted on one person or on seven, with an optional correction from a person's earlier run or from early scalp and eye readings: eight tasks in all ([the model](../models/README.md)). |
| [`walking-landmarks/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/walking-landmarks/) | Where will six skin markers go? Change the speed, the step rate or the muscle signals of an invented walker and see where six forecasts put both ankles, knees and wrists 200 milliseconds later, in 3D. [Try the shared model on one marker](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/shared-motion/#point-motion) · [See recorded marker travel](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/Interoceptomics/stride-signals/) · [Offline viewer](../models/walking-landmarks.zip) |
| [`elbow-cue/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/elbow-cue/) | The elbow after a cue to bend or straighten it: compare a forecast of the elbow sensor from the cue and its recent readings with one that also reads scalp electrode C3. To give the shared model an instruction to move the right arm, [type a cue](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/shared-motion/#cued-arm). [Read the study](papers/cued-arm/) · [Find the sensors in Interoceptomics](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/Interoceptomics/scalp-and-arm/) · [Offline page](elbow-cue-offline.zip) |
| [`arm-transfer/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/arm-transfer/) | Cued arm movements in new people: compare a small transformer's forecasts of three sensors, and the average change for each cue, with what five people outside the fitting group did. [Try a first-run correction](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/shared-motion/#arm-transfer) · [Read the study](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/papers/arm-transfer/) · [Offline reader](arm-transfer-offline.zip) |
| [`reach-feedback/one-week/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/reach-feedback/one-week/) | The reach-feedback models run, unchanged, on the same macaque a week later: choose a recorded reach and an electrode contact, change a hand, elbow or handle coordinate, and compare forecasts of the spikes in the next 100 milliseconds made with and without the latest movement; a second page follows 39 muscle–tendon paths of the original researchers' arm model. [Follow the muscle–tendon paths](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/reach-feedback/one-week/muscle-paths/) · [Read the study](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/papers/reach-feedback/one-week/) · [Replay the arm in 3D in Interoceptomics](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/Interoceptomics/reach-feedback/one-week/) · [Offline reader](reach-feedback/one-week-offline.zip) |
| [`reach-feedback/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/reach-feedback/) | A macaque's reach, with the brain's touch area recorded: choose one of four recorded reaches, shift the hand's last positions or add spikes to one unit, and compare forecasts of the next 100 milliseconds of movement, and of the spikes in the 100 milliseconds after, with what was recorded. [Read the study](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/papers/reach-feedback/) · [Open the 3D replay in Interoceptomics](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/Interoceptomics/reach-feedback/) · [Offline reader](reach-feedback-offline.zip) |
| [`cylinder-rotation/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/cylinder-rotation/) | A sensor on a carried cylinder: choose a recorded trip and a moment in it, edit an earlier acceleration reading, and compare forecasts of how fast the cylinder will turn in the next tenth of a second with what the sensor recorded. [Read the study](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/papers/cylinder-rotation/) · [Turn the cylinder in 3D in Interoceptomics](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/Interoceptomics/cylinder-rotation/) · [Offline reader](cylinder-rotation-offline.zip) |
| [`target-reach/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/target-reach/) | A cylinder carried to one of nine targets: choose a hand and a recorded trial, change the destination, and compare forecasts made from 200 milliseconds of its tracked movement on two clocks, one started at the first camera sample and one once it had travelled 15 mm. [Read the study](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/papers/target-reach/) · [Follow the cylinder in 3D in Interoceptomics](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/Interoceptomics/target-reach/) · [Offline reader](target-reach-offline.zip) |
| [`contact-forecast/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/contact-forecast/) | The brain's touch area of one macaque on two days: choose a day, a trial and one of the electrode contacts, and compare a forecast of the events it records in the next 100 milliseconds, made by models fitted on the first day, with the count recorded, or edit a copy of the history. [Read the study](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/papers/contact-forecast/) · [Rotate the recorded arm in Interoceptomics](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/Interoceptomics/contact-forecast/) · [Offline reader](contact-forecast-offline.zip) |
| [`cortical-reach/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/cortical-reach/) | A macaque's arm, pushed by a robot and then reaching: pause one recorded trial at the push or the reach, or invent the handle's movement and the earlier spikes, and compare forecasts of the handle's next 100 milliseconds with and without spikes from the brain's touch area. [Read the study](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/papers/cortical-reach/) · [Rotate the measured arm in Interoceptomics](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/Interoceptomics/cortical-reach/) · [Offline reader](cortical-reach-offline.zip) |
| [`muscle-spindle/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/muscle-spindle/) | A rat's stretched muscle and one of its sensory nerve fibres: step through a recorded stretch, or invent the pull on the tendon, the motor's movement and the earlier spikes, and compare forecasts of the spikes in the next 20 milliseconds with those counted. [Read the study](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/papers/muscle-spindle/) · [See inside a muscle spindle in Interoceptomics](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/Interoceptomics/muscle-spindle/) · [Offline reader](muscle-spindle-offline.zip) |
| [`cross-limb-movement/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/cross-limb-movement/) | A lifting wrist and a balancing body: change an invented history of the marker and the muscles and compare the forecast of the next 125 ms from one small transformer that learned both tasks with those of models that each learned one. [Offline reader](cross-limb-movement-offline.zip) |
| [`cross-limb-controls/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/cross-limb-controls/) | The same forecasts from straight-line fits that the general model's program runs, fitted on both studies or on one, beside simple rules such as continuing the recent movement; turn the invented history's axes and the forecast turns with them. |
| [`muscle-and-motion/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/muscle-and-motion/) | Leg muscles and the pelvis on a beam: change an invented muscle signal or movement and compare one small transformer's forecast of the next 125 ms with two that each forecast one. [Offline reader](muscle-and-motion-offline.zip) |
| [`muscle-motion-controls/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/muscle-motion-controls/) | The same two forecasts from straight-line fits that the general model's program runs: learned from walking alone, from a few standing examples alone, or from walking and then those standing examples. |
| [`visual-balance/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/visual-balance/) | Balance on a beam: change an invented movement or electrode signal and compare a small transformer's forecasts, with and without the scalp, of how far the head and the base of the spine will move in the next eighth of a second after the view rotates, then the errors on six new people. [Try the general model](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/visual-balance-controls/) · [Study](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/papers/visual-balance/) · [Offline reader](visual-balance-offline.zip) |
| [`visual-balance-controls/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/visual-balance-controls/) | The same forecast from the general model: its shared part as it was, with a final step fitted with all the electrodes, without the scalp, or with the part of the scalp signal that the eye and muscle signals predict taken out, beside a straight-line fit on the movement alone. Change an invented eye signal and how much of it reaches the scalp. [Study](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/papers/visual-balance/) |
| [`walking-instructions/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/walking-instructions/) | Two walking instructions: keep an invented walk's last 200 milliseconds fixed, switch between "as usual" and "fast but not running", and see where a small transformer expects the pelvis and the right heel a tenth of a second later, then the errors on recorded walks. [Try the general model](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/walking-instruction-controls/) · [Study](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/papers/walking-instructions/) · [Offline reader](walking-instructions-offline.zip) |
| [`walking-instruction-controls/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/walking-instruction-controls/) | The same forecast from the general model, with forward set by the walker's own travel: its shared part as it was, with a final step fitted with or without the instruction, beside straight-line fits, an untrained copy and simpler rules. Turn the heading, or switch the output between the walker's axes and the laboratory's. [Study](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/papers/walking-instructions/) |
| [`heel-and-force/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/heel-and-force/) | One step on a force plate: change an invented step's heel movement, the time since the heel struck and the size of a shin muscle's signal, and compare a transformer that forecasts both where the heel will be and how hard the foot will press a tenth of a second later with two that each forecast one, then the errors on recorded walks. [Try the general model](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/shared-heel-and-force/) · [Study](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/papers/heel-and-force/) · [Offline reader](heel-and-force-offline.zip) |
| [`shared-heel-and-force/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/shared-heel-and-force/) | The same two forecasts from the general model: its shared part as it was, with a final step that forecasts both from two combinations of its inputs, one without that limit, and straight-line fits and simpler rules beside them. Change the heel's forward travel, the time since the heel struck and the shin muscle's signal. [Study](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/papers/heel-and-force/) |
| [`pedal-load/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/pedal-load/) | A pedal that cannot move: change an invented trace of its load and of the shin muscle's electrical signal, swap in another recording's muscle signal, and compare forecasts of the pedal's reading a tenth of a second later, with the errors on two new people. [Try the general model](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/shared-pedal-load/) · [Study](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/papers/pedal-load/) · [Offline reader](pedal-load-offline.zip) |
| [`shared-pedal-load/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/shared-pedal-load/) | The same forecast from the general model: its shared part as it was, with a final step fitted for the pedal, beside straight-line fits, an untrained copy and a response model. Change the pedal's trend and the size and timing of a muscle burst. [Study](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/papers/pedal-load/) |
| [`muscle-tracking/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/muscle-tracking/) | A muscle in the shin, filmed by ultrasound: choose or type an invented history of a bundle's length and angle, swap in other angles, and compare eight forecasts of how much longer or shorter it will look ten tracking steps later, with the errors on four new people. [Try the general model](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/shared-muscle-tracking/) · [Study](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/papers/muscle-tracking/) · [Offline reader](muscle-tracking-offline.zip) |
| [`shared-muscle-tracking/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/shared-muscle-tracking/) | The same forecast from the general model: its shared part as it was, with a final step fitted for the shin muscle, beside straight-line fits, an untrained copy and a calculation from the bundle's geometry. Change an invented length and angle history. [Study](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/papers/muscle-tracking/) |
| [`back-rotation/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/back-rotation/) | A sensor on the back: choose walking or standing and the readings the model may use, change an invented history, and see a small transformer's forecast of how many degrees the sensor will turn in the next tenth of a second, with and without two grids of electrodes on the skin over the spine, then the errors on three new people. [Try the general model](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/shared-back-rotation/) · [Study](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/papers/back-rotation/) · [Offline reader](back-rotation-offline.zip) |
| [`shared-back-rotation/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/shared-back-rotation/) | The same forecast from the general model: its shared part as it was, with a final step fitted for the back sensor, beside carrying the last turn forward and a straight-line fit. Change an invented history of turns and voltages. [Study](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/papers/back-rotation/) |
| [`cervical-forecast/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/cervical-forecast/) | The neck after a pulse at the wrist: change the early readings of an invented example and compare a small transformer's forecasts of the neck electrode's voltage 12 to 14 milliseconds after the pulse, with and without the recording at the armpit, then see how the forecasts did on six new people. [Study](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/papers/cervical-forecast/) · [Offline reader](cervical-forecast-offline.zip) |
| [`neck-voltage/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/neck-voltage/) | The same forecast as the general model's program runs it: a straight-line correction to the last neck reading, from the neck alone, with the scalp, thumb and chest, or with the armpit as well. [Study](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/papers/cervical-forecast/) |
| [`scalp-forecast/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/scalp-forecast/) | Scalp and eye readings in arm forecasts: compare forecasts of three arm sensors from the cue and early movement, with and without six scalp electrodes or three around the eyes, with the recorded test. [Try the eye adjustment](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/shared-motion/#early-signals) · [Read the study](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/papers/scalp-forecast/) · [Offline reader](scalp-forecast-offline.zip) |
| [`finger-transfer/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/finger-transfer/) | Does a finger forecast carry over to a new person? Run the five-person model, which groups the brain-surface electrodes by the brain area each sat over, and see each person's scores from the turn in which they were the one left out. [Offline reader and model](../models/finger-transfer.zip) |
| [`walking-force/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/walking-force/) | One stride, two force plates: change an invented muscle signal and compare six fitted models of the load two plates in the floor record as a person walks. [Right-foot plate model](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/shared-motion/#right-plate) · [Study and figures](papers/muscle-and-floor/) · [PDF](papers/muscle-and-floor/muscle-and-floor.pdf) · [Offline viewer](../models/walking-force.zip) |
| [`knee-moment/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/knee-moment/) | What turning moment follows a step? Estimate how hard the forces around each knee push it to bend or straighten, from the previous four seconds of joint angles. [Offline reader](../models/knee-moment.zip) |
| [`finger-motion/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/finger-motion/) | Change the finger named on the screen and an invented brain-surface rhythm, and see how six fitted models of one person's glove forecast how much each finger will move. [Offline reader](../models/finger-motion.zip) |
| [`finger-signals/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/finger-signals/) | Give invented glove readings, a finger cue and a level of brain-surface activity to two fitted models of one person's glove, one of which also reads the brain signal, and see how each forecasts the five fingers 120 ms ahead; beside them, what adding the brain recording did on the recorded trials. [Offline reader](../models/finger-signals.zip) |
| [`knee-stride/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/knee-stride/) | Follow both knees through four seconds of an invented walk, see which part of the previous stride the forecast copies, and compare the corrections trained for the knees with the general model's, 15 frames ahead. | [`gait-rhythm/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/gait-rhythm/) | Compare dominant leg-muscle and knee-angle rhythms for 11 walks, or calculate the spectra from compatible local recordings. [Offline reader and study](../models/gait-rhythm.zip) |

| [`stride/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/stride/) | Give the model half a second of a measured walk or run. It predicts the next 0.60 seconds at 18 points on the body. Turn the figure, follow one foot and reveal where its markers landed. |
| [`population-motion/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/population-motion/) | Step through one recorded trip and compare how far a rat moved with forecasts that use its earlier movement alone or also use firing from two brain regions. |
| [`word-motion/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/word-motion/) | Type **walk** or **run** to generate a short stride. Rotate the 18 body points and compare them with a measured training example ([the model and its study](../models/word-motion/)). |
| [`whole-body/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/whole-body/) | Three recorded whole-body movements, a scoop, a jump and a hop, to turn in 3D. No model runs on them. |
| [`papers/current/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/papers/current/) | The four papers, to read online. |
| [`papers/language-and-observed-movement/`](https://eliminatenoise.github.io/NeuroTranslation/papers/language-and-observed-movement/language-and-movement.html) | A separate four-page supplement on finding a recorded movement from words, with its PDF and source. |
| `launchers/` | Desktop shortcuts to NeuroTranslator. |
| `preview.html` | An old address. It forwards to the start page. |

NeuroTranslator is built from [`demo/`](../demo/README.md). Change it there and rebuild; do not edit the built files here. [`build-manifest.json`](build-manifest.json) names the build this folder holds.

Offline copies of the readers are listed in [LAUNCHERS.md](../LAUNCHERS.md); `hand-search/`, `shared-motion/`, `whole-body/` and `word-motion/` each open offline as a single saved page, with launchers in their folders. The stride and three-rat downloads also include offline viewers and launchers, and so do the ZIPs of `walking-landmarks/`, `elbow-cue/`, `arm-transfer/`, `scalp-forecast/`, `cervical-forecast/`, `back-rotation/`, `muscle-tracking/`, `pedal-load/`, `heel-and-force/`, `walking-instructions/`, `cross-limb-movement/`, `muscle-and-motion/`, `visual-balance/`, `muscle-spindle/`, `cortical-reach/`, `contact-forecast/`, `target-reach/`, `cylinder-rotation/`, `reach-feedback/` and `reach-feedback/one-week/`. The numbers behind them are on [the studies page](../benchmarks/README.md). Who made each recording, and under which licence: [RIGHTS.md](RIGHTS.md).
